authors: Allan Dickens Ouga; Henry Mwanaki Alinaitwe; Godfrey Mwesige
title: Modelling Block Laying Productivity on Building Sites in Kampala
journal: Journal of Construction in Developing Countries 25(1): 109-128
access: Open access, CC BY 4.0 (licence text seen on PDF p.1; Crossref also lists CC BY 4.0)
activity: Solid concrete block laying, block 400 x 225 x 200 mm (11 blocks/m2), work height 0.5-5.5 m, individual block layer with porters
model_type: OLS multiple linear regression (Model 3 of 4 candidate models, chosen by adjusted R2 and AIC)
output_unit: m2 of blockwork per block layer per hour

variables.name: H
variables.unit: m (work height, mid-value of height band)

variables.name: P
variables.unit: number of porters per block layer

variables.name: EXED
variables.unit: dimensionless
variables.coding: EX x ED; 1 if experience >= 5 years AND craft/diploma qualification, else 0

validity_range_text: Kampala building sites; work heights not exceeding 6 m above ground (Table 2 range 0.5-5.5 m); block size 400 x 225 x 200 mm; P observed 1-4 with 44 of 70 observations at 2 porters (abstract p.109; Table 2 p.116)
location_in_paper: Eq. 3 p.119; Table 2 p.116; Table 3 p.120
limitations: Individual mason, not crew; per-hour output, no per-day model; P has little internal variability; EX and ED individually not significant; text inconsistent on block size used for model development (p.113-114 vs p.119) and on n (70 / 83 / 160); no hold-out validation seen; concrete blocks in Uganda, not clay brick in India; no weather, mortar, bond or crew-size variables; R2 0.65 leaves 35% unexplained

authors: M. K. Parthasarathy; R. Murugasan; Ramya Vasan
title: Modelling manpower and equipment productivity in tall residential building projects in developing countries
journal: Journal of the South African Institution of Civil Engineering 60(2): 23-33 (Paper 1547)
access: Free full text (SciELO South Africa PDF); no licence text seen, so not marked open access
country: India (52 tall residential projects, various locations)
activity: Blockwork (block type and thickness not reported) in framed RCC residential buildings >= 30 m tall, tower crane and hoist assisted; monthly project-level data over 18 months
model_type: Multiple linear regression of monthly blockwork quantity on man-days and equipment hours (Model 10, all months); monsoon and non-monsoon variants Models 11 and 12
output_name: Blockwork quantity per project per month
output_unit: m2 per month (project level, NOT per mason or crew)

variables.name: H
variables.unit: m (mean of start-of-month and end-of-month building height at which work was done)

variables.name: MD
variables.unit: man-days per month

variables.name: TCH
variables.unit: tower crane hours per month allocated to blockwork (10% share)

variables.name: HH
variables.unit: hoist hours per month

validity_range_text: Tall (>= 30 m) framed RCC residential projects in India with tower crane and hoist, floor-to-floor height 3-4 m; predictor ranges from Table 1 p.25 (H range 3-174 m is the overall range listed in Table 1; BW 34-5141 m2/month, mean 2605); SE 374.08 m2 quoted, no RMSE
location_in_paper: Models 10-12 p.29; Table 1 p.25; Tables 3-4 pp.29-30
limitations: Dependent variable is monthly quantity, so MD coefficient (0.183 m2 per man-day) is confounded with crane and hoist hours (VIF 14.885) and must not be read as mason productivity; tall buildings only; block type and thickness not reported; crane-hour allocation to blockwork by project judgement; validation by scatter plot only (Figure 4), no numerical hold-out metric; Table 1 labels man-days as MH for blockwork

title: Modelling masonry labour productivity using multiple regression
journal: Proceedings of the 30th Annual ARCOM Conference, 1-3 September 2014, Portsmouth, UK, pp. 1345-1354 (no DOI)
access: Free full text on ARCOM website; no licence text seen, not marked open access
country: India (Kerala; two high-rise RCC projects with masonry infill)
activity: Laterite block masonry in stretcher bond, subcontract and directly employed crews, 8 h day 6 days/week; walls below and above 2.2 m and with numerous corners
model_type: Stepwise multiple linear regression (SPSS) on log10-transformed productivity; 152 crew-day observations; 70/30 split-sample validation
equation_text: Equation not printed in the paper; Table 2 (unstandardised B) gives the coefficients. Reconstructed (inference from Table 2 + text that log10 of the dependent variable was used): log10(P) = -0.348 + 0.157*ModeEmp - 0.024*OT - 0.220*WC3 - 0.178*WC2 - 0.024*DelayMat, so P = 10^(...). Back-transformation is not printed in the paper.
output_name: Masonry labour productivity (assumed log10 of value in m2/man-hr; back-transformed output in m2 per man-hour)
output_unit: m2 per man-hour (model is fitted on log10 of this)

variables.name: ModeEmp
variables.unit: dimensionless

variables.name: OT
variables.unit: hours of overtime per day
variables.coding: continuous; subcontract crews rarely > 1 h, directly employed mean 3.7 h with two observations of 8 and 9 h; min 0 inferred from statement that overtime was on 85% / 94% of observations

variables.name: WC3
variables.unit: dimensionless
variables.coding: 1 = walls higher than 2.2 m (work content 3), else 0; reference is WC1

variables.name: WC2
variables.unit: dimensionless
variables.coding: 1 = walls with numerous corners, height < 2.2 m (work content 2), else 0; reference is WC1 straight walls < 2.2 m

variables.name: DelayMat
variables.unit: hours per day lost to material unavailability
variables.coding: continuous; 0 when no delay; 30 min to 5 h on 57 of 152 observations

validity_range_text: Two Kerala high-rise sites, laterite blocks; observed productivity 0.12-1.09 m2/man-hr (mean 0.41); overtime 0-9 h/day; material delay 0-5 h/day; adjusted R2 0.787; split-sample MSE 0.0117 (model-building) vs MSPR 0.0119 (validation) in log10 units (inference); Durbin-Watson 1.855
location_in_paper: Table 1 p.1348; Table 2 p.1350; validation pp.1351-1352; observed range p.1347
limitations: Two sites only; laterite blocks not clay brick; block size and wall thickness not reported; weather variables not significant (masonry considered interior); 152 crew-days from two sites; overtime effect driven largely by directly employed labour on one site; log10 back-transformation not stated; RMSE/MAPE not reported (MSE in log units only); work content limited to three classes

authors: Saja H. Rasool; Faiq M. S. Al-Zwainy
title: Estimating Productivity of Brickwork item using Logistic and Multiple Regression Approaches
journal: Scholars Journal of Engineering and Technology (SJET) 4(5): 234-243
access: Free PDF on publisher site (saspublishers.com); no licence text seen, not marked open access; no DOI found
activity: Brickwork productivity; brick type, wall thickness and crew not reported; 50 observations taken from a 2012 University of Baghdad thesis
model_type: Multiple linear regression (SPSS Enter method). A binary logistic model is also printed in the paper but predicts P(good productivity), not a rate, and is not entered here.

variables.name: X1
variables.unit: years (age of worker)

variables.name: X2
variables.unit: years (experience)

variables.name: X3
variables.unit: number of workers

variables.name: X4
variables.unit: level of execution, listed as 'Meter' in Table 1 (undefined)

validity_range_text: Predictor ranges from Table 2 (p.237). Calibration R 0.682, R2 0.466, adjusted R2 0.418 (Table 5). MAPE 7.5% (and R2 0.7619 / R 87.28%) is from a check on only 5 new observations (Tables 12, 14, 16). y mean 3.95, SD 0.5076 (Table 3). Site security variable constant and dropped.
location_in_paper: Eq. 3 p.238; Tables 2-3 pp.237-238; Table 5-6 p.239; Table 16 p.242
limitations: Unit of productivity not stated anywhere; secondhand data (2011/2012 thesis); n = 50; only age and level significant; experience sign inconsistent; Table 2 and Table 3 give different means for X3 and X4; validation on 5 points; no weather, material or wall variables; equation reproduces the paper's own Table 14 values (derived check)

authors: Paikun Paikun; Cici Fatimah; Nadhya Susilo Nugroho; Dody Kusmana
title: Labor Productivity Rating Model for Light Brick Wall Installation in Residential Projects
access: Free PDF; licence CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 listed in Crossref metadata (licence text not seen in the PDF text)
activity: Lightweight (light brick, probably AAC) wall installation by a crew of 2 masons + 1 helper on one housing project; wall thickness and unit size not reported
model_type: OLS multiple linear regression of daily crew output on effective working minutes of each crew member (productivity-rating / labour utilisation approach)
output_name: Wall area installed per day by the 3-person crew
output_unit: m2 per day (crew of 2 masons + 1 helper)

variables.name: X1
variables.unit: minutes per day (effective working time of craftsman I)

variables.name: X2
variables.unit: minutes per day (effective working time of craftsman II)

variables.name: X3
variables.unit: minutes per day (effective working time of helper)

validity_range_text: One crew, 20 working days; Y1 observed 18.95-19.41 m2/day; predictor ranges 10-20 minutes wide (Table 5). MAPE 0.66% (accuracy 99.34%) is in-sample (Table 8), and the recap on p.268 says 99.43%.
limitations: Derived check: applying the printed 3-decimal coefficients to Table 5 inputs gives 19.27-19.64 m2/day (observed 18.95-19.41), MAPE about 1.5%; an OLS refit of Table 5 reproduces intercept 6.302 and R2 0.850 with slopes 0.01775, 0.01083, 0.00762. Table 8 model values are not in day order (rows 1 and 10 have identical inputs but different values). Single crew, single site; effective time is an outcome not a planning input; X3 not significant; no weather, height or wall variables; in-sample accuracy only

title: Study of relationship between rework and labor productivity in Building Construction Projects
access: Free PDF (held in project folder); no licence text seen, not marked open access
activity: Brick works, productivity of a 2-labourer crew; project-level averages from 40 building projects 2015-2018
model_type: Simple linear regression (single predictor: rework cost)
output_name: Labour productivity in brick works (2-labour crew)

variables.name: X
variables.unit: % of item contract price (rework cost in brick works)

validity_range_text: Mean rework cost 4.51% and mean productivity 26.2 m2/day (p.37); Figure 2 x-axis spans 0-10% but data min/max not printed; West Bank building projects 2015-2018
location_in_paper: Eq. 5 and Table 5 p.37; Figure 2 p.38
limitations: Single predictor; project-average productivity; crew size, wall type and unit size not controlled; rework cost is known only after the fact so it acts as a scenario input; text mislabels variables (Equation 3 defines Y as rework cost and X as productivity, and one sentence says block works instead of brick works); MAPE and RMSE not reported
